summary: Radar 2026-10-18. Three things are moving fastest. (1) The bootleg "reta" story is still building. Futurism (Oct 17), the AJC (Oct 15) and Medscape's piece on the Reddit side-effects study (Oct 15) are all covering it. CBS reports the FDA received 2 death reports after people used products sold as retatrutide, and the FDA would not say whether it verified them. This is our #1 proven lane, at 179 views. (2) People are searching for the status of named next-gen drugs: "is retatrutide approved", "new eli lilly weight loss drug" and "what drug was just approved". That fits the dated status question that works on Instagram, plus the orforglipron EU recommendation (CHMP backed it on Oct 16; the Commission decision is pending). (3) New tirzepatide heart data. A SURPASS-CVOT heart-failure subgroup (AJMC, Oct 15) found death or heart-failure events in 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide. That makes a clean "Does Mounjaro…?" question. For the evergreen slots, the SURMOUNT-5 head-to-head follow-up and the "why some lose 20%" question are refreshed by Yahoo Creators and GoodRx pieces. I lowered the scare topics. The Wegovy "eye stroke" headline is a resurfaced March 2026 FAERS study, and scare topics about approved drugs underperform for us. "Does tirzepatide cause cancer" searches are only worth a calm explainer. I could not verify the ScienceAlert "fat cells self-destruct" story, so it's flagged caution and low. Switching-how-to, anorexia/telehealth loophole and compounded-source stories stay rejected. Release timing: the Oct 29 Lilly earnings are a likely retatrutide/orforglipron news spike. Have the status Shorts live before then.

candidates.topic: Is 'reta' sold online the same as Lilly's retatrutide? FDA logged 2 death reports linked to products sold as retatrutide (unverified, per CBS); Lilly calls them black-market, not trial drug
candidates.angle: Calm 'what's confirmed vs not' Short. Retatrutide is investigational as of Oct 2026, and no regulator has approved it. Lilly's CMO says the black-market product is 'not a medicine'. Point to a prescriber. Never name sellers.

candidates.topic: Does tirzepatide (Mounjaro) help people with type 2 diabetes and heart failure? SURPASS-CVOT subgroup: death or heart-failure events 18.2% on tirzepatide vs 21.5% on dulaglutide
candidates.angle: Drug-first plain question, answered within 10 s. This was an exploratory subgroup of the SURPASS-CVOT trial (adults with type 2 diabetes plus atherosclerotic heart disease and a history of heart failure, about 4 years). The comparator was dulaglutide, not placebo, and the result was 'associated with' a 17% lower relative risk. Mention the FDA's August 2026 heart-event indication, attributed and dated.
